requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

CSS comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.css.fingerprints` has no implementation edges and no review roots. Each of its clauses specifies observable behavior only:

- "Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`". This fixes the digest value. A different SHA-256 library, or a different code path that gives identical digests, still conforms. The encoding rules themselves belong to the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`. That requirement is only context here, and its own assessment covers it.
- "The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`". This is an observable value: the scheme string the CSS provider reports. The `OutlineLang::fingerprint_scheme` signature and the `OutlineContent` accessors are prescribed by the cited requirement, not by this subject. Any way of producing the string satisfies this clause.
- "CSS comments are excluded from structural hashes". This is observable: a comment edit leaves the hash unchanged. A comment filter in the parser, in the hasher, or in a post-pass would all give the same behavior.

The subject text prescribes no library, type, signature, field, or delegation interface that a behavior-preserving alternative would violate. No implementation root is needed, and a test would supply the evidence for the behavior.

behavioral: No gap found. I did not need implementation source. The obligations come from `requirements.sdk.sources.css.fingerprints`. The cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme` only supply context, so I did not reassess their own tests.

1. **SHA-256 digest.**
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has a CSS case, `a.css` with `rule[a]`.
   - It asserts the structural hash is 64 characters long and all hex digits.
   - The exact digest value and the "unambiguous encoding" are not asserted. These are implementation choices, and the word-boundary check below covers the observable effect.

2. **Whitespace-separated words, with whitespace never hashed and each word encoded separately.**
   - The same CSS case compares `a { /* note */ content: "two words"; }` with `content: "two   words"`. The hashes must be equal, so extra whitespace does not matter.
   - It also compares against `content: "twowords"` and asserts the hashes differ. This is the `ab cd` versus `abcd` boundary.

3. **CSS comments excluded.**
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has the `a.css` case on `rule[a]`.
   - It checks that changing the comment text gives an equal hash. It checks that removing the comment gives an equal hash. It checks that changing the non-comment word `red` to `blue` gives a different hash, so the comparison is not vacuous.
   - The `bundled_fingerprints_…` CSS case also changes the comment text from `note` to `edited` and expects an equal hash.

4. **Fingerprint scheme identifies the rules and version.**
   - `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` calls `check(languages::Css, …, "css-structural-v1")`.
   - The `check` helper asserts `language.fingerprint_scheme()` and `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` both equal `css-structural-v1`.
   - It also asserts that the loaded `OutlineContent` retains that scheme through `inferred.fingerprint_scheme()`.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no CSS-specific boundary the text names that is left unasserted, and no acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
CSS comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
